predictions.selection_reason: dialect parameter -> conditional PostgreSQL escaping -> potentially insufficient SQL injection protection
predictions.source_summary: dialect parameter flows from Sequelize constructor options through Utils.format() -> SqlString.format() -> SqlString.escape()
predictions.sink_summary: Escaped string values are returned for SQL query construction, used in database operations
predictions.guard_summary: PostgreSQL uses single quote escaping (''), other dialects use backslash escaping; both methods are database-specific escaping controls
predictions.risk_pattern: Different SQL injection escaping rules applied based on dialect parameter, potentially insufficient if dialect detection is incorrect or bypassed
predictions.context_summary: The added condition changes SQL string escaping behavior: PostgreSQL uses double single-quotes for escaping, while other databases use backslash escaping for control characters and quotes
unresolved_facts: How dialect parameter is validated/sanitized before reaching SqlString.escape
Whether there are other code paths that call SqlString.escape directly without dialect parameter
Whether the dialect detection mechanism can be bypassed or manipulated

retrieval_query.mechanism_summary: Improper neutralization of SQL special elements due to conditional escaping based on dialect
retrieval_query.missing_control: consistent SQL escaping across all database dialects
retrieval_query.mechanism_keywords: sql injection, neutralization, escaping, dialect, conditional

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')
top_sast_rules.description: Building a database query from user-controlled sources is vulnerable to insertion of malicious code by the user.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement secure coding practices specific to CWE-090. Review OWASP guidelines and CWE documentation for detailed mitigation strategies.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
top_sast_rules.description: When escaping special characters using a meta-character like backslash or ampersand, the meta-character has to be escaped first to avoid double-escaping, and conversely it has to be unescaped last to avoid double-unescaping.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Detect output operations that lack proper encoding for the target context
top_sast_rules.remediation: Use context-appropriate encoding for all output operations. Implement proper escaping for HTML, JavaScript, CSS, and URL contexts.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')
top_sast_rules.description: Externally influenced data changes the syntax or meaning of a command sent to a downstream command interpreter.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-77 command-injection command-construction shell exec spawn process subprocess child_process os.system popen argument-delimiter metacharacter
top_sast_rules.remediation: Keep external data separate from command syntax and use safe argument APIs.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior
top_sast_rules.description: Conditional comments are an IE-specific feature and not portable.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement secure coding practices specific to CWE-758. Review OWASP guidelines and CWE documentation for detailed mitigation strategies.

top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
